neighbours.label: the result clause of a 'so ... that' or 'such ... that' (so busy that you could, so popular that ticket sales had to, in such quantities that it required), as opposed to the same facts with no result clause
fire: The market was so crowded that you could barely move.
The talks were so popular that seats had to be added.
It was produced in such amounts that it required new rules.
He has been fired more times than you can count on your fingers.
The noise was so loud that nobody could sleep.
The soup was so hot that it burned my tongue.
Her debts grew so large that she had to sell the house.
It rained so much that the roads were closed.
quiet: The market was crowded and you could buy fruit.
The talks were popular with the older members.
It was produced in a small plant near the coast.
He has been fired twice and lives with his mother.
The noise was loud and came from the garage.
The soup was hot and tasted of pepper.
Her debts grew and she sold the house.
It rained in the night and the roads were wet.

notes: The peak is usually on the verb of the result clause ('could', 'refused', 'required'), so 'so' itself may not be the trigger.
